what_it_does: This chip performs biochemical reactions—like PCR (amplifying DNA) or gene assembly—at 384 different sites in parallel, each at its own precise temperature. The challenge is that silicon conducts heat easily, so it's hard to keep one corner of the chip hot while another stays cool. The solution uses special structures built into the silicon substrate and independent temperature sensors and heaters for each site, so reactions can run simultaneously at different temperatures without interfering with each other.
